root_cause.text: The omap_mpuio_driver was registered from the probe callback of another driver (omap_gpio_probe) while holding the device lock, violating driver core locking rules and causing a potential deadlock, and it was never unregistered on module exit.
root_cause.evidence: The commit description states: "it neither makes sense to register drivers from probe() callbacks of other drivers, nor does the driver core allow registering drivers with a device lock already being held." It also notes: "the omap_mpuio_driver is never unregistered from the driver core, even if the module is unloaded." The patch moves registration from omap_mpuio_init() (called in probe) to the module initcall and adds proper unregistration in module_exit.

candidates.rationale: This function is called from the probe callback of omap_gpio_probe while holding the device lock, leading to potential deadlock when registering another driver.
Part of the init function that performs setup under the device lock, contributing to the problematic registration context.
Directly registers the mpuio driver from within the probe of another driver, violating driver core locking rules and causing a potential deadlock.
Registers the mpuio device under the same locked context, compounding the deadlock risk.
This is the only unregister action in the module exit function; omap_mpuio_driver and device are never unregistered, causing resource leak and potential issues on module removal.
